template.source: MarsMen · Adrien batch 01 · 1:1 two-photo day tags (Wildhorn c0126 validated, run-1 #11)
template.production_method: real photo + pasted product — two side-by-side photos of the same woman's ankles (A25 photo method, one generation, two panels), dark headline band, day tags, pouch + glass pasted bottom centre, tiny disclaimer by script
template.refusal_risk: low (template is a phallic joke with pitcher plants; ours is ankles in sandals — nothing suggestive)

decode.scroll_stop_trick: A black band shouting a 'X doesn't matter, Y does!' twist over two photos that look identical at first glance until the day tags make you compare them — the eye hunts for the difference.
decode.angle_carried: 'Size doesn't matter, thickness does' (sexual innuendo, day 0 / day 90) — Adrien's run-1 keep: 'Size doesn't matter… unless it's your belly!'
decode.hidden_reading: what you obsess over is the wrong number — the ad changes the metric the buyer judges herself by
decode.scene_logic: two near-identical nature photos with a before/after reading; ours = the same sandals, the same feet, the same floor, two days apart: strap biting into a puffy ankle vs strap loose on a slim ankle
decode.visual_trick: the twin-photo repetition — same framing, same light, only the subject's volume changes; copy literally
decode.shape_or_function_equivalent: pitcher plant (swollen → thick) ↔ ankle and calf (swollen → slim); two rival bottles pasted at the bottom ↔ our pouch + a clear glass with the tablet fizzing, same spot, same scale
decode.render_style: photoreal, daylight, green/outdoor in the template → ours a bright bathroom-tile or wooden floor, consistent across both panels
decode.text_treatment: ALL CAPS white condensed bold on a black top band, day tags in white caps on black rounded chips, tiny '*RESULT MAY VARY' bottom-left

strategy.angle: A8-L heavy, swollen legs — 'the scale doesn't matter, swollen legs do'
strategy.mechanism: M1: when the body can't clear everyday oxidative stress, the tissue in the legs stays inflamed and stops draining normally, so fluid sits there — heavy, tender, puffy — and no diet reaches it, because it was never fat; the tablet turns a glass of water into hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is, reaches the tissue and helps the body switch that process off so normal drainage can resume
strategy.sub_avatar: trigger: sandal straps and sock marks dig in by evening · cause: inflamed tissue holding fluid · tried: dieting harder, weighing herself, water tablets
strategy.belief_installed: It was never fat. It's fluid my body stopped clearing — and no diet reaches it.

people.customer_look: only feet and ankles of woman 40–55, soft midlife build, ordinary clothes, visibly swollen heavy calves and ankles (sock marks, puffy ankles) — never a young fitness model — no face

visual_bans: no bare torso, no pitcher plant, nothing phallic — ankles and sandals only
both panels are the same person, sandals and floor; only the ankle volume changes
the product is only ever a white effervescent tablet in a clear glass of water — no other dosage form, no blister pack, no sachet
no bottle, jar or tub for Edenvia — the container is the stand-up pouch of Image 1, label untouched
any glass holds clear water with fine rising bubbles; never hot water, tea or coffee in that glass
no competitor brand name, logo or bottle shape anywhere (brand.json banned list)
no disease or drug name on the image
compliance_flags: before/after photo of a body part: results claim — keep '*RESULTS MAY VARY'
_note: Adrien's run-1 kept this template with 'Size doesn't matter… unless it's your belly!' after Loom 2 said the first twist was not logical; ours keeps the formula and names the real problem.
